Aman Chaudhary, J
1.

The present petition has been filed for quashing of FIR No.341, dated 16.07.2019, registered under Sections 120-B, 323, 406, 420 IPC (Section 379-B IPC added later on), at Police Station Shahabad,
District Kurukshetra and all other consequential proceedings arising therefrom on the basis of the compromise dated 10.02.2022.

2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and also gone through the case file.
3.

This Court while issuing notice of motion vide order dated 10.10.2022, directed the parties to appear before the trial Court/Illaqa Magistrate for recording their statements with regard to the compromise.
4. Pursuant to the aforesaid order, report dated 09.01.2023 has been received from the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Kurukshetra.

A perusal of the said report reveals that statements of the concerned persons have been recorded in the present case, who have stated that the integrity of this order/judgment CRM-M-46068-2022 (O&M) 2023:PHHC:107761 matter has been settled between them and they have no objection in case the FIR in question is quashed.

The compromise effected Jasveer Singh @ Jasbir Yadav vs State Of Haryana And Another on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3753274/
1 between them is genuine, without any undue influence and coercion.

None of the accused have been declared as proclaimed offender.

5. The Full Bench of this Court in Kulwinder Singh and others vs. State of Punjab, 2007 (3) RCR (Criminal) 1052, held that High Court has power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. to allow the compounding of non-compoundable offence and quash the prosecution where the High Court is of the view that the same was required to prevent the abuse of the process of law or otherwise to secure the ends of justice.

entities.text: Kulwinder Singh and others vs. State of Punjab, 2007 (3) RCR (Criminal) 1052
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This power of quashing is not confined to matrimonial disputes alone.

6. Hon'ble the Supreme Court of India in the case of Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and another,
2012 (4) RCR (Criminal) 543, had observed that in order to secure the ends of justice or to prevent the abuse of process of Court, inherent power can be used by this Court to quash criminal proceedings in which a compromise has been effected.

entities.text:
Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and another,
2012 (4) RCR (Criminal) 543
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant portion of para 57 of the said judgment reads thus:-
"57.

The position that emerges from the above discussion can be summarised thus:
the power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences under Section 320 of the Code.

Inherent power is of wide plenitude with no statutory limitation but it has to be exercised in accord with the guideline engrafted in such power viz; (i) to secure the ends of justice or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court.

XXX---XXX"
7. Hon'ble The Supreme Court of India in case of Jayrajsingh Digvijaysingh Rana vs. State of Gujrat and another, 2012(12) SCC integrity of this order/judgment CRM-M-46068-2022 (O&M)
2023:PHHC:107761 401, held that where there is a partial compromise with some of the accused even then also the proceedings against the said accused should be quashed as the same would not even remotely result in his conviction.

entities.text: Jayrajsingh Digvijaysingh Rana vs. State of Gujrat and another, 2012(12) SCC integrity
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. In view of the afore-referred judgments, perusing the report of the trial Court regarding amicable settlement between the petitioner and the complainant, this Court finds that quashing the FIR will accord a quietus to all disputes between the parties and it is in the interest of both sides to bury the hatchet and lead a peaceful life.
Thus, no useful purpose would be served in continuing the proceedings and in order to secure the ends of justice, the criminal proceedings in the present case deserve to be quashed.

9. Resultantly, the present petition is allowed and FIR No.341, dated 16.07.2019, registered under Sections 120-B, 323, 406, 420 IPC (Section 379-B IPC added later on), at Police Station Shahabad,
District Kurukshetra and all other consequential proceedings arising therefrom are quashed qua the petitioner on the basis of the compromise dated 10.02.2022.
